client: Hi Luna, I've been really struggling since my grandmother passed away last month. Every time I go to her favorite coffee shop, it just hits me like a wave of sadness, and I feel completely overwhelmed. I’m not sure if talking about it will really help, but I don’t know what else to do.
therapist:
Hi there. I can really sense how deeply you’re feeling the loss of your grandmother, especially when you visit that coffee shop. It sounds like it brings back a flood of emotions, and I want you to know that it’s completely understandable to feel overwhelmed during such a difficult time.

Grief can be very intense, and it’s normal to feel a mix of sadness and confusion about how to cope with it. It seems like there's a part of you that might be hesitant to talk about your feelings, perhaps wondering if it will really help. But sharing your thoughts and reminiscing about your grandmother can often provide a sense of connection and relief, even if it feels daunting right now.

What do you think it might be like to share some of your memories or feelings about her? It could be a way to honor her memory while also giving yourself the space to process your emotions. Remember, you don’t have to go through this alone. I'm here to support you.
vocal_descriptors: very high pitch, loud, fast speech
